findings.description: The previous/next chat chords (Ctrl+Shift+]/[) produced no selection move in the lab configuration while Ctrl+PageDown moved it positively; chord families must be re-evidenced positively per configuration (F1 a11y N6).

A fresh-profile promo modal swallows all keyboard input until dismissed; Escape is the verified dismissal, so first-run scenes carry a defensive capture-then-Escape block that is a no-op when the modal is absent (the rc.14 lesson).
Destructive confirmation modals must confine Tab/Shift+Tab focus to their actions and close on scoped Escape, returning focus to the surface that opened them (the d19 trap-ladder contract).

guard.guard: the d19 trap-ladder lab evidence and the tab/shift-tab KeyBindings

findings.description: Opening the terminal dock starts a live PTY, but keyboard focus does not transfer to it on open; typed input keeps landing on the previously focused surface (F1 a11y N5, carried to the F2 a11y binding items).

Digit-family chords carry shifted-symbol companions (for example alt+^ beside Ctrl+Alt+Shift+6/7) that must be exercised alongside the primary chord: a binding whose listener answers only one form dispatches the other into the void (the N6 family + the d25 Gate-B missing-listener lesson).

guard.guard: the d24/d25 gate scenes exercise the companion form on every digit chord, and the seam tests pin the listener form, not just the binding
